raw_response:
I'm a 50-year-old woman farming 10.9 mu here in Quzhou. My husband works at a factory in town, so most days it's just me and my mother-in-law handling the fields. My daughter is away at university and my son is in middle school. We don't have much cash to spare, so I have to watch every yuan. I've been farming this land for 20 years, wheat and maize double crop, same as most people around here.

The wheat went in last October, around the 10th. I used Jinmai 47, same seed I've used for three years now. Cost me about 40 yuan per mu. Before planting, I plowed the field and put down about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu — that's one bag per mu, 15-15-15. In March when the wheat turned green, I topdressed about 20 kg of urea per mu. The wheat looks pretty good right now, nice and green, better than last year actually. I'll irrigate it once more at heading time in early May, and if June is dry, I'll water again at grain filling. Each irrigation costs me diesel money for the pump, about 40 yuan per mu, so I don't water more than I have to — but I also don't want to lose yield. I sprayed herbicide in March, and if I see rust or aphids I'll spray fungicide or insecticide, but so far it looks clean. I hire a combine for harvest in early June, about 60 yuan per mu. I expect around 400 kg per mu, same as my average.

For the summer maize, I'll plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid right after wheat harvest in mid-June. The window is tight — sometimes only five or six days between harvest and planting. I either do a quick rotavator pass or hire a custom no-till planter if I'm running late. Seed costs about 50 yuan per mu. At planting, I put down about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu. Then at the big trumpet stage in July, I topdress about 18 kg of urea per mu. I'll irrigate twice — once at trumpet stage and once at grain filling in August if it doesn't rain. Maize usually brings me 450 kg per mu, sometimes 500 if the weather cooperates. I spray herbicide after emergence and insecticide if I see borers.

I have to balance everything against what I can afford. Seed, fertilizer, diesel for the pump, pesticides, and hiring the combine — it all adds up to about 8,000 to 9,000 yuan for the year. I can't spend more than that or I won't have enough for my son's school fees and my mother-in-law's blood pressure medicine. Some years I think about putting on more fertilizer, but then I think — last year's amount was fine, why risk the cash? Better to be a little safe. My neighbor with the 20-mu farm puts on more fertilizer and gets slightly better yield, but he's got more land and his son helps full-time. I can't copy him exactly.
